The core innovation lies in the introduction of a flow function that aggregates information for training intermediate states, enabling the model to update its parameters using partial trajectory segments and receive intermediate learning signals. This approach is designed to reduce gradient variance and improve the efficiency of the sampling process. The empirical results show that DGFS outperforms several existing methods, such as Path Integral Sampler (PIS) and Denoising Diffusion Sampler (DDS), in terms of lower gradient variance and better sampling performance. The introduction of the flow function and the subtrajectory balance loss adds to the model architecture and training process, requiring the training of an additional neural network and the computation of a more complex loss function. This increased complexity is a valid concern, as it could pose practical challenges for researchers and practitioners looking to adopt the method. The paper should clearly articulate the novel aspects of DGFS and how it addresses the limitations of existing methods.
